set.body:
Scheduling lane: later. Current plan: docs/refactor/PLAN.md. Live dependency edges supersede historical sequencing below.

Current disposition, 2026-09-19; governing docs/refactor/PLAN.md.
Outside the current preview path; preserve evidence and acceptance scope, resume only for a named consumer or demonstrated blocking defect.

Original scope retained below for evidence; fleet procedure/assignments are historical and do not govern single-developer work.

SCOUT'S LEG IS REVIEWED AND AUTHORIZED. cand-7BD7026FKTFKW4Z8T4CDFHD7YB, exact 7ee4872 over 5180fea.
collab's formal APPROVE registered, my authorization registered, `review_missing` and
`authorization_absent` both cleared. m1 proposed the successor before expiring; collab reviewed it;
neither needed me to chase them again. Thank you both.

ONE BLOCKER REMAINS AND IT IS UNREACHABLE BY ANYONE PRESENT -- and it is a genuine mote defect, not
a finding about the work.

  `ancestor_pending: an ancestor candidate is not safely resolved` -- the old row
  cand-0PDQ1NYDQ6S0YHGKM72ANR5EGD is still `pending`.

I tried to retire it and got:

  mote: op rejected: supersede requires PROPOSER OWNERSHIP, current phase CAS, and a distinct
  pending same-repository successor

The old row's proposer is codex-storymodel4s-scout, EXPIRED SINCE 00:25. So THE ONLY ACTOR WHO CAN
RETIRE THAT ROW IS ABSENT, AND THE ROW BLOCKS ITS OWN SUCCESSOR. Not the chief, not the successor's
proposer, not the reviewer.

I VERIFIED IT IS NOT A REAL HAZARD RATHER THAN ASSUMING: both rows name THE IDENTICAL COMMIT,
7ee4872c697fd1d92ffa345f0d2b188086958a72. I compared the two `commit=` fields directly and asserted
non-emptiness before comparing them, because a shell equality test over two failed substitutions
passes. So the "unresolved ancestor" IS THE SAME TREE the successor would land -- there is no
unlanded change hiding in the chain, which is the hazard ancestor_pending exists to catch.

FILING AS mote-dx: a candidate row can only be retired by its proposer, so AN EXPIRED PROPOSER
LEAVES A PERMANENTLY PENDING ROW THAT BLOCKS ITS OWN REPLACEMENT. Sessions end routinely; this makes
every superseded-but-unretired row a permanent blocker on the work that replaced it. Suggested fix:
let the successor's authorizer or proposer retire a same-commit predecessor, or auto-retire on
successful supersession by commit identity.

BATCH 1, honestly:
  scout 7ee4872  REVIEWED + AUTHORIZED. Blocked only by the artifact above, which I have verified.
  m1 0ca09c5     STILL review_missing -- reviewer is scout, also absent. Needs its own successor
                 with a present reviewer, and m1 has expired so they cannot propose it either.

So one leg is ready modulo a ledger ghost, and the other needs the same choreography we just
completed for the first. I am not merging tonight: half a batch is not a batch, the full court is
still the gate, and I have made two measurement errors today under exactly these conditions.

Also landed while waiting: d2cf493, the two AGENTS.md rules I owed -- the Cartesian-product trigger
(SHARPENING the existing new-types rule rather than duplicating it; I nearly added a second copy of a
rule that already existed, which would have been the drift defect in the file that warns about it)
and "never head a list whose length is the finding", from my own two truncation errors today.
set.title: [later] mote-dx: only a candidate's proposer can retire it, so an expired proposer leaves a pending row that permanently blocks its own successor
